title: Delete Operation for Two Strings
summary: Given two strings word1 and word2, determine the minimum number of steps required to make them identical.
statement: Given two strings word1 and word2, determine the minimum number of steps required to make them identical. In one step, you can delete exactly one character from either string.
constraints: Each operation deletes one character from either word.
hints: Keeping a common subsequence avoids deleting its characters.
Either compute LCS, or directly compute the edit cost for every prefix pair.
Use DP: equal chars copy diagonal; otherwise one plus min(delete from either word).
The prefix recurrence considers the last operation of an optimal deletion sequence.
editorial: The prefix recurrence considers the last operation of an optimal deletion sequence.

tests.explanation: Keep the common subsequence ea; delete s and t for two operations.
The longest shared subsequence has four characters, leaving four deletions.
